get.description: Returns up to 20 customers per call in `customers`. `pagination` gives you `total`, the number of customers across all pages; `has_next`, which is `true` when there is another page; and `next_page`, the URL of that page. Parameter names are case-sensitive. An unknown or wrongly cased name, such as `firstName`, `max` or `postcode`, is rejected with `400 unknown_parameter`, and `errors[0]` in the response names the parameter. `createdFrom`, `createdTo`, `updatedFrom` and `updatedTo` are accepted but ignored: they do not narrow the results. Listed customers do not include `custom_properties`; to get them, use [Retrieve a customer](/api-reference/customers/retrieve-a-customer).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of customers per page, up to `20`. A larger value is treated as `20`; `pagination.limit` shows the value used.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of customers to skip. If you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` is used.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at `1`. Each page holds `limit` customers.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search. You can also send it as `searchText`, `query` or `keyword`.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Filters customers by email address.

parameters.name: companyName
parameters.description: Filters customers by company name.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: Filters customers by phone number.

parameters.name: mobile
parameters.description: Filters customers by mobile number.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Filters customers by country.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filters customers by state.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Filters customers by city.

parameters.name: postCode
parameters.description: Filters customers by post code. The name is case-sensitive: `postcode` is rejected with `400 unknown_parameter`.

parameters.name: customerGroup
parameters.description: Filters customers by customer group.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Returns only customers with this status: `active`, `inactive`, `pending`, `approval_awaiting` or `awaiting_verification`. Letter case does not matter. Any other value is rejected with `400`, and the error message lists the allowed values.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort the results by. An unknown field is rejected with `400 invalid_sort_field`.

200.description: `customers` holds up to `limit` customers, and `pagination` holds `total`, `has_next` and `next_page`.

400.description: Rejected because a parameter name is unknown or wrongly cased (`unknown_parameter`), the `sort` field is unknown (`invalid_sort_field`), or `status` is not one of the five allowed values.

post.description: Creates a customer from the fields you send in the `customer` object and returns `201` with the new customer. Use its `customer_id`, not its `internal_id`, in later calls. `first_name` is required. `status` must be `active`, `inactive`, `pending`, `approval_awaiting` or `awaiting_verification`. If you leave `status` out, the API creates the customer as `awaiting_verification` with no usable password, even if you sent one. For that customer, [Change a password](/api-reference/customers/change-a-password) returns `401`, even straight after [Reset a password](/api-reference/customers/reset-a-password). To create a customer who can sign in, send `status: "active"` together with `password`. To create a company, send `company: true` and `company_name`. The response includes `company_name` but not `company`. The API accepts address fields placed directly on the customer, such as `address1`, `suburb` and `postcode`, but does not save them. To save addresses, use [Add addresses](/api-reference/customers/add-addresses). The response always lists three addresses, `primary`, `shipping` and `billing`, even when you sent none. If no address was saved, all three are blank. `primary` and `billing` have the same address `id`, so they are one saved address.

201.description: The customer was created. Returns the new customer in `customer`, including its `customer_id`.

400.description: The request is invalid. For example, a missing `first_name` returns the message `Customer name is required`.

409.description: Another customer already uses this email address. This includes deleted customers. The message is `Provided email already registered`.

put.description: Updates a customer and returns `200` with the updated customer. Inside the `customer` object, send only the fields you want to change. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Sending `custom_properties` replaces the customer's whole list, so include every entry you want to keep. Leave `custom_properties` out to keep the list unchanged. Send each entry as `{label, description}`. The API also accepts `{name, value}`, but the response always uses `label` and `description`. An entry keeps its own `id` (the entry's, not the customer's) while its `label` and `description` stay the same; new text gets a new entry `id`. You can set `store_credit` directly, but the API does not record the change in the customer's store credit history. The balance can then differ from the total of the recorded adjustments. To record a change, use [Adjust store credit](/api-reference/customers/adjust-store-credit).

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: The `customer_id` of the customer to update. Do not send its `internal_id`: that number can also be another customer's `customer_id`, so the call can update the wrong customer.

200.description: The customer was updated. Returns the updated customer in `customer`.

404.description: No customer has that `customer_id`.

delete.description: Deletes a customer and returns `204` with no body. The API moves the customer to the trash; it does not erase the record. [Retrieve a customer](/api-reference/customers/retrieve-a-customer) still returns it, with `is_in_trash: true`. Its email address stays registered: [Create a customer](/api-reference/customers/create-a-customer) rejects that address with `409`, and [Check an email address](/api-reference/customers/check-an-email-address) returns `exists: true` for it. [Export customers](/api-reference/customers/export-customers) leaves deleted customers out. You cannot restore a deleted customer through the API; use the WebCommander admin interface. Deleting the same customer again returns `404` with the message `Customer already in trash`.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: The `customer_id` of the customer to delete. Do not send its `internal_id`: that number can also be another customer's `customer_id`, so the call can delete the wrong customer.

404.description: No customer has that `customer_id`, or the customer is already in the trash. In the second case, the message is `Customer already in trash`.

get.description: Returns up to 20 of the store's order custom fields under `order_custom_fields`, each with 12 keys; [Retrieve an order custom field](/api-reference/order-custom-fields/retrieve-an-order-custom-field) returns all 21. `pagination` gives the total number of matching fields and the page you are on, and `group_meta` marks the list read-only with `writable: false`. Send `filterBy` to keep one field type, `sort` and `dir` to order the fields, and `field_metadata=true` to add a description of each key. `q`, `search`, `name`, `label`, `is_active` and unknown parameters are accepted and ignored: no parameter searches the fields.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Fields per page. The default and the maximum are `20`: a larger value is capped at `20`, and `pagination.limit` shows `20`. `0`, a negative number and text are rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of fields to skip. When you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` wins. A negative number or text is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number, read as `offset = (page - 1) * limit` against the limit the store applied: `page=2` alone skips 20 fields, and `limit=5&page=3` skips 10. `page=0` returns the first page. A negative number or text is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort the fields by: `id`, `label`, `name`, `type`, `orderNo`, `isActive`, `created` or `updated`. `type`, `orderNo`, `isActive`, `created` and `updated` sort by `field_type`, `order_no`, `is_active`, `created_on` and `last_updated_on`, in that order. Those five response key names, a leading `-` and any other value are rejected with `400`. An empty value is ignored.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The sort direction: `asc` or `desc`, in any letter case, such as `DESC`. A value such as `sideways` is rejected with `400` and the message `dir: must be one of: asc, desc`. An empty value is ignored.

parameters.name: filterBy
parameters.description: Keeps only the fields of this type, and sets `pagination.total` to their number. Send the type exactly as `field_type` shows it, in lower case. `LONGTEXT`, or any value that is not one of the ten types, is rejected with `400`. An empty value is ignored.

parameters.name: field_metadata
parameters.description: Send `true` or `1` to add `field_metadata`, which describes an order custom field's keys, including all 12 that a listed field has: each key's type and, for some keys, the allowed values or the maximum length. `false` and `0` add nothing. Any other value, including `True` and `TRUE`, is rejected with `400`.

200.description: The fields on this page under `order_custom_fields`, `pagination` with the total and the page size, and `group_meta`, which shows `writable: false`. With `field_metadata=true`, the response also has a `field_metadata` key. The response has no `ETag` or `Last-Modified` header.

field_metadata.description: Only when you send `field_metadata=true` or `1`.

400.description: You sent a value the listing rejects. `limit=0` is rejected with the message `'limit' must be a positive integer`. A negative or non-numeric `limit`, `offset` or `page` is rejected with `'<name>' must be a non-negative integer` and `details[0].code` set to `invalid_integer`. A `sort` other than the eight accepted values is rejected with `sort: must be one of: id, label, name, type, orderNo, isActive, created, updated` and `details[0].code` set to `invalid_value`. A `dir` such as `sideways` is rejected with `dir: must be one of: asc, desc`. A `filterBy` that is not one of the ten field types is rejected with `details[0].code` set to `invalid_enum`. A `field_metadata` other than `true`, `false`, `1` or `0` is rejected with `field_metadata must be true/false or 0/1` and `details[0].code` set to `invalid_boolean`. You also get this `400` when the call just before this one on the same client was rejected for one of these parameters, including a `filterBy` rejected by [Count order custom fields](/api-reference/order-custom-fields/count-order-custom-fields) and a `field_metadata` rejected by [Retrieve an order custom field](/api-reference/order-custom-fields/retrieve-an-order-custom-field); send the call again.

post.summary: Add a product to a cart
post.description: Adds a product to the cart named by `session_id`, creating the cart if needed, and returns the whole cart under `cart`. Send the product's `id` as `product_id`, a `quantity`, and the customer's `internal_id` as `customer_id`, at the top level of the body. If you leave out `session_id`, the store names the cart with your HTTP session's `JSESSIONID` cookie value, and `cart.session_id` in the response shows that name. Adding a product that is already in the cart raises that cart item's `quantity` and keeps its `id`.

201.description: The cart under `cart`, with the `customer_id` you sent. The response has no `group_meta`. When your request sends no `JSESSIONID` cookie, the response sets one in a `Set-Cookie` header. If the product needs options and you send none, the call also returns `201`, but the body is not valid JSON: it has `"status": "incomplete-info"` instead of `cart`.

400.description: `customer_id` or `quantity` is missing: the message is `customer_id not found` or `quantity not found`. You sent the customer's `customer_id` instead of the customer's `internal_id`: the message is `No Customer Found`. A deleted product can still appear in [List stock at an inventory location](/api-reference/inventory-locations/list-stock-at-an-inventory-location). The cart would hold more of the product than its stock: the message is `f:<n> quantity of this product is not available`. Carts do not reserve stock, so this limit applies to each cart on its own.

get.description: Returns your categories in `categories`, from every level of the tree in one list, 20 per call unless you send a lower `limit`. Categories in the trash are left out, and the most recently updated come first unless you send `sort`. Narrow the list with `name`, `searchText` and `parent`; a category must match every filter you send. Query parameters the listing does not know, such as `q` or `search`, are ignored instead of rejected.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of categories per page. Defaults to `20`, which is also the most you can get: a larger value is capped at `20`, and `pagination.limit` shows the value applied. `0`, negative values and values that are not numbers are rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of categories to skip. When you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` wins.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A 1-based page number, read as `offset = (page - 1) * limit` against the `limit` applied, so `page=2` alone skips 20 categories. `pagination.next_page` and `pagination.previous_page` use `offset`, not `page`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort by: `id`, `name`, `title`, `sku`, `url`, `created` or `updated`. Values such as `created_on`, `last_updated_on` and `-id` are rejected with `400`. Sorting by `name` ignores letter case. Without `sort`, the most recently updated categories come first. `dir` defaults to `desc`, so `sort=name` alone sorts Z to A.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The sort direction: `asc` or `desc`, in any letter case. Defaults to `desc`. Any other value is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Keeps only categories whose name contains this text, in any letter case.

parameters.name: searchText
parameters.description: Keeps only categories whose name or `sku` contains this text, in any letter case. Every `sku` the store generates starts with `CATEGORY-`, so a value such as `cat` matches every category whose `sku` the store generated.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The parent category's `id`. Keeps only that category's children, and `0` keeps none. A value that is not a number returns `500`.

get.description: Returns up to 20 blog posts under `blogs`, latest `date` first, with `group_meta` and a `pagination` block that holds the total and the links to the next and previous pages. Filter with `ids`, `category` and `visibility`, change the order with `sort` and `dir`, and send `page` or `offset` to get the next page. Any query parameter other than the ten on this page is rejected with `400`. After the listing rejects `limit=0`, a `sort` or a `dir`, your next request on the same client returns that same `400`, even when its own parameters are valid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of blog posts per page. The default and the maximum are `20`: a larger value is capped at `20`, and `pagination.limit` shows `20`. `0` is rejected with `400` and the message `'limit' must be a positive integer`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of blog posts to skip.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, counting from `1`. The store reads it as `offset = (page - 1) * limit`. `page=0` returns the first page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort the blog posts by: `id`, `name`, `url`, `date`, `created` or `updated`. Without `sort`, the posts come latest `date` first. Any other value, including `title`, `created_on` and `last_updated_on`, is rejected with `400` and the message `Sort field not exist`.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The sort direction: `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `desc`. Any other value is rejected with `400` and the message `Sort order must be asc or desc`.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Keeps only the blog posts whose `id` you list. Repeat the parameter for each post, as in `ids=1201&ids=1202`. A comma list such as `ids=1201,1202` returns `500`, and a bracketed name such as `ids[]=1201` is rejected with `400`. A post in the trash is never returned.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Keeps only the blog posts filed under the blog category whose `id` you send. A blog category `id` that no post is filed under, or that matches no blog category, returns no posts and no error.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Keeps only the blog posts with this `visibility`: `open`, `hidden` or `restricted`, in any letter case. Any other value returns no posts instead of an error.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Accepted, but it filters nothing: the listing returns the same posts whatever you send.

parameters.name: field_metadata
parameters.description: Send `true` to add a `field_metadata` key that describes each of the seventeen fields of a blog post. Takes `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; any other value, `True` included, is rejected with `400` and the message `field_metadata must be true/false or 0/1`.

200.description: The blog posts on this page under `blogs`, `group_meta`, and `pagination` with the total, the page size and the links to the next and previous pages. With `field_metadata=true`, a `field_metadata` key is added that describes each field. Posts in the trash are not listed. The response has no `ETag` or `Last-Modified` header.

field_metadata.description: Only when you send `field_metadata=true`.

blogs.title: Spring Sale Announcement
blogs.content: Save up to 40% on selected products until the end of the month.

400.description: The listing rejected a query parameter. A parameter it does not accept, including a bracketed name such as `ids[]`, returns `unknown query parameter(s): <name>` with `details[0].code` set to `unknown_parameter`. `limit=0` returns `'limit' must be a positive integer`, with `details[0].code` set to `out_of_range`. A `sort` it does not accept returns `Sort field not exist`, with the reason `invalid_sort_field`, and a `dir` other than `asc` or `desc` returns `Sort order must be asc or desc`. A `field_metadata` other than `true`, `false`, `1` or `0` returns `field_metadata must be true/false or 0/1`, with `details[0].code` set to `invalid_boolean`.

500.description: `ids` was sent as a comma list, such as `ids=1201,1202`. Repeat the parameter instead: `ids=1201&ids=1202`. The body has no `error` object: it is `{"status": "error", "code": 500, "message": "Unexpected Error Occurred"}`.

get.description: Returns up to 20 blog categories under `blog_categories`, ordered by `name` and ignoring letter case, and `pagination` with the total and the links to the next and previous pages. Send `sort` and `dir` to change the order, and `page` or `offset` to get the next page. Only `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `sort`, `dir` and `field_metadata` are accepted; any other parameter, such as `q` or `name`, is rejected with `400`. After a rejected `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `sort` or `dir`, your next request on the same client returns that same `400`, even when its own parameters are valid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of blog categories per page. The default and the maximum are `20`: a larger value is capped at `20`, and `pagination.limit` shows `20`. `0` is rejected with `400` and the message `'limit' must be a positive integer`. A negative number, or a value that is not a number such as `abc`, is rejected with `400` and the message `'limit' must be a non-negative integer`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of blog categories to skip. When you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` wins. A negative number, or a value that is not a number such as `abc`, is rejected with `400` and the message `'offset' must be a non-negative integer`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number, read as `offset = (page - 1) * limit` against the limit the store applied. `page=2` alone skips 20 categories; `limit=1&page=2` skips 1. A page past the last category returns no categories. A negative number, or a value that is not a number such as `abc`, is rejected with `400` and the message `'page' must be a non-negative integer`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: What to sort the blog categories by: `id`, `name`, `url`, `description`, `created` or `updated`. Without `sort`, the categories are ordered by `name`, ignoring letter case. Any other value, such as `Name` or `-id`, is rejected with `400` and the message `Sort field not exist`. So are `created_on` and `last_updated_on`, although a blog category has fields with those names. To reverse the order, send `dir=desc`.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The sort direction: `asc` or `desc`, in lower case. `dir=desc` without `sort` lists the categories by `name` in reverse. `DESC`, `Desc` or any other capitalised form is not rejected, but the store ignores it and returns the categories in ascending order. Any other value, such as `sideways`, is rejected with `400` and the message `Sort order must be asc or desc`.

parameters.name: field_metadata
parameters.description: Accepted, but adds nothing: the response still has only `blog_categories` and `pagination`.

200.description: The blog categories on this page under `blog_categories`, and `pagination` with the total, the page size and links to the next and previous pages. `field_metadata=true` adds no key. The response has no `ETag` or `Last-Modified` header.

400.description: The listing rejected a query parameter, and the message says which. A parameter it does not accept returns `unknown query parameter(s): <name>`, with `details[0].field` naming the parameter and `details[0].code` set to `unknown_parameter`. A `sort` value it does not accept returns `Sort field not exist`, with `details[0].code` set to `invalid_sort_field`. A `dir` other than `asc` or `desc` in any letter case, such as `sideways`, returns `Sort order must be asc or desc`, with an empty `details`. `limit=0` returns `'limit' must be a positive integer`, with `details[0].code` set to `out_of_range`, and a negative or non-numeric `limit` returns `'limit' must be a non-negative integer`, with `details[0].code` set to `invalid_integer`. A negative or non-numeric `offset` returns `'offset' must be a non-negative integer`, and a negative or non-numeric `page` returns `'page' must be a non-negative integer`, each with `details[0].code` set to `invalid_integer`. After a rejected `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `sort` or `dir`, your next request on the same client returns this `400` too; send that request again.

get.description: Returns the variation types in ascending order of each type's `id`, 20 per call unless you send `limit`. Each type comes with every one of its options. `pagination` gives the number of matching types in `total`, and `has_next` is `true` while another page follows. Send `search` to keep only types whose `name` contains that text, and `standard` to keep only one kind of type. Any query parameter not listed here is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: standard
parameters.description: Keeps only types of this kind: `text`, `color` or `image`, in any letter case. Any other value is rejected with `400` and the reason `invalid_enum`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of types per page, from `1` to `100`. Defaults to `20`. `pagination.limit` shows the value applied. `0`, values above `100` and text such as `abc` are rejected with `400` and the message `must be a whole number from 1 to 100`. 200.description: The variation types on this page in `variations`, and `pagination` with `total`, `limit`, `offset`, `has_previous` and `has_next`. With `field_metadata=true`, a `field_metadata` key is added between them. The response has no `ETag` or `Last-Modified` header.

get.description: Returns your store's countries in ascending `id` order, 20 per call unless you send `limit`. Send `code`, `name` or `id` to find one country by its exact value, or `search` to match part of a `name` or `code`; filters you send together must all match. Send `sort` and `order` to change the order. `dir`, `q`, `field_metadata` and other parameters the listing does not know, except `page`, are ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of countries per page, from `1` to `100`, or `all` (in any letter case) for every row from `offset` on. Defaults to `20`. `pagination.limit` shows the page size applied; with `all` it shows the number of rows returned. `0`, `-1`, `101` and text other than `all` are rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of countries to skip. A negative value is rejected with `400`. An `offset` past the last row returns no rows, the full `total`, `has_previous` set to `true` and `has_next` set to `false`.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Keeps only the country with this two-letter `code`, in any letter case. A value that is not two letters is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Keeps only the country with exactly this `name`, in any letter case. Part of a name matches nothing; use `search` for that.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Keeps only the country whose `id` is this number.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Keeps only countries whose `name` or `code` contains this text, in any letter case. `gb` finds United Kingdom by its code. A value of only spaces applies no filter.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: `true` keeps only active countries and `false` only inactive ones, in any letter case. Any other value, `1` included, is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by: `id`, `name` or `code`. Defaults to `id`. `name` sorts without regard to letter case. Any other value, `state_count` included, is rejected with `400`.

Without `sort`, they come in ascending order of the currency's `id`, and the base currency is not moved to the top. Send `search` to find currencies by `name` or `code`, and `active` to keep only active or inactive ones. `page` is rejected with `400`; `q`, `base` and any other unknown query parameter are ignored and do not filter the listing.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The sort direction: `asc` or `desc`. Any other value is rejected with `400`. `order` is accepted as another name for `dir`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of currencies per page, from `1` to `100`. Defaults to `20`. `pagination.limit` shows the value applied. `0` and values above `100` are rejected with `400` and the message `must be a whole number from 1 to 100`.

parameters.name: offset

get.summary: List the records of a transaction
get.description: Send `type` to choose the kind of record, such as `product` or `category`; the call is rejected with `400` without it. Records come newest first, 20 per call unless you send `limit`, which takes `1` to `200`; `sort` and `order` are ignored. With `detail=slim`, the default, each item has the record's `id` and a few fields that depend on `type`; with `detail=full`, each item is the record as its own retrieve call returns it. A type with no records stamped, or a number no record is stamped with, returns `200` with an empty `items` list and a `total` of `0`, not `404`.

parameters.name: transaction_no
parameters.description: The transaction number, exactly as it was sent on the create call that stamped it, in the same letter case, such as `IMPORT-2026-0001`. A listing row returns it in `transaction_no`. The SDKs percent-encode it for you, so `#`, `%`, spaces and non-ASCII letters reach the store intact. A number that contains `/` cannot be read.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Required. The kind of record to list, one of the 15 `type` names in lower case: `product`, `product_variation`, `product_review`, `customer`, `order`, `category`, `currency`, `country_tax`, `country_tax_state_rule`, `custom_tax_profile`, `custom_tax_rule`, `custom_tax_rule_zone`, `shipping_profile`, `shipping_rule`, `shipping_rate`. A missing `type` is rejected with `400`. A name in upper case, an unknown name or a comma-separated list is rejected with `400` too.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of records per page. Defaults to `20`. `max` is accepted as another name for `limit`. Takes `1` to `200`. A value above `200` is rejected with `400` and the message `max cannot exceed 200`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of records to skip. A negative value is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of records to return, counting from `1`. It sets `offset` to `(page - 1) * limit`. Text such as `abc` is rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: `slim`, the default, returns a short form of each record: its `id` and a few fields that depend on `type`, such as `name`, `sku` and `url` for a product. `full` returns each record as its own retrieve call returns it, without the wrapping key. Any other value, `FULL` included, is rejected with `400` and the message `detail must be 'slim' or 'full'`.

200.description: The number in `transaction_no`, the `type` you sent, the records on this page in `items`, and `pagination` with ten keys. The response has no `ETag` header.

transaction_no.description: The number you sent in the path.

type.description: The `type` you sent.

items.description: With `detail=slim`, each item has the record's `id` and the short fields for its `type`. With `detail=full`, each item is the record's full body, which differs by `type`.

400.description: `type` is missing: the message is `type query parameter is required`. Or `type` is not one of the 15 names in lower case: the message starts `Invalid type '<value>'. Allowed:` and lists the 15 names. Or `detail` is not `slim` or `full`: the message is `detail must be 'slim' or 'full'`. Or `limit` is above `200`: the message is `max cannot exceed 200`, with one `details` entry for `max`. Or `limit`, `offset` or `page` is not accepted, as on [List transactions](/api-reference/transactions/list-transactions). The `error.code` is `invalid_request`.

ProductInformation.description: Each product card, and how the product listing displays, pages and sorts.

list.description: Columns per row in list view.

allow_user_per_page.description: Let visitors change the number of products per page.

per_load.description: Products fetched each time a visitor loads more.

CheckoutPageSettings.description: All six sections, as [Get checkout page settings](/api-reference/checkout-page/get-checkout-page-settings) returns them.

billing_address.description: The billing address form's active field keys. Read-only.

shipping_address.description: The shipping address form's active field keys. Read-only.

fields.description: Each form field, inactive fields included.

active.description: Whether the field shows on the form.

required.description: Whether the customer must fill in the field.

order.description: The field's position on the form.

CheckoutCustomerCheckout.description: How customers sign in, sign up or check out as a guest. At least one of `allow_sign_in`, `allow_sign_up` and `checkout_as_guest` must stay on.

allow_sign_in.description: Let returning customers sign in during checkout.

newsletter_subscription.description: Show a newsletter opt-in on the checkout page.

CheckoutSignUp.description: Whether customers can, or must, create an account during checkout.

enabled.description: Let customers create an account during checkout.

required.description: Make customers create an account to place an order.

CheckoutGuestCheckout.description: Whether customers can order without an account.

enabled.description: Let customers order without an account.

quick_signup.description: Offer guests a one-click account creation.

enable_delivery_service.description: Offer on-demand delivery: a delivery date picker shows at checkout.

CheckoutOrderSummary.description: What the checkout's order summary shows.

show_product_thumbnail.description: Show product images in the order summary.

show_quantity.description: Show the quantity column or label.

enable_payment_expand_view.description: Expand the payment section by default.

order_confirm_captcha.description: Ask for a CAPTCHA before the order is confirmed.

show_logo.description: Show the store logo on the checkout page.

custom_html.description: Custom HTML shown on the checkout page.

enabled.description: Let customers add a comment to their order.

send_notification.description: Email staff when an order comment is added. Reads `false` while `enabled` is `false`.

CheckoutTermsAndCondition.description: Whether customers must accept terms and conditions before ordering, and where the terms are.

enabled.description: Make customers accept the terms and conditions before ordering.

text.description: The text shown before the terms link.

link_label.description: The text of the terms link.

type.description: Where the terms come from: `page`, `link` or `text`.

CheckoutTermsReference.description: Where the terms are. Holds only the one key that matches `type`.

page.description: The terms page, when `type` is `page`: an object with the page's `id` and the page's `name`.

link.description: The URL of the terms, when `type` is `link`.

CheckoutGroupMeta.description: One entry per section. Only [Get checkout page settings](/api-reference/checkout-page/get-checkout-page-settings) and [Update checkout page settings](/api-reference/checkout-page/update-checkout-page-settings) return it.

kind.description: What the section is. `setting` for all six sections.

writable.description: Whether you can write to the section. `false` for `billing_address` and `shipping_address`, `true` for the other four.

href.description: The section's own path, such as `/api/v4/admin/settings/page_settings/checkout_page/order_summary`.

description.description: What the field does.

type.description: The kind of value the field takes: `boolean`, `string`, `enum`, `array` for an address section's `fields`, or `resource` for an address section on `/checkout_page`.

default.description: The field's default value.

allowed_values.description: The values the field accepts. `others.terms_and_condition.type` is the one `enum` field and lists `page`, `link` and `text`.

max_length.description: The longest value accepted, for a `string` field.

required.description: `true` when the field must have a value. On `/checkout_page`, `others.login_url` is the one field marked required.

read_only.description: `true` when you cannot write the field or section.

href.description: For an address section on `/checkout_page`: the section's own path, such as `/api/v4/admin/settings/page_settings/checkout_page/billing_address`.

item_schema.description: For an address section's `fields`: a description of each of the six keys of a field record.

catalog.description: For an address section's `fields`: every field key the form can use.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `method_not_allowed`.

details.description: One entry per rejected field. Empty when the error is not about a field.

field.description: The field that was rejected.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `required` or `constraint_violation`.

value.description: The value you sent, when the API includes it.

request_id.description: The id the store gave this request.

ProductPageSettings.description: The product page settings, one key per section.

ProductPageConfiguration.description: What the product page itself shows, in four blocks.

ProductPageActionButtons.description: Which buttons the product page shows.

display_add_to_compare_button.description: Show the Add to Compare button.

display_add_to_wishlist_button.description: Show the Add to Wishlist button.

display_tax_with_expect_to_pay_price.description: Show tax with the expect to pay price.

twitter.description: Offer sharing on Twitter. Depends on `configuration.social_sharing.enable_share_on_social_media`.

copy_link.description: Offer a button that copies the product link.

display_title.description: Show a title beside the share buttons.

tabular_view.description: Turn on the tabular view. Depends on `allow_viewers_to_change_display_mode` in the same section.

ProductPageReviewCapabilities.description: What the product review plugin offers. Read-only.

available.description: Whether the product review plugin is installed. Read-only: a write that changes it is rejected with `400` and the code `read_only`.

display_add_to_compare_button.description: Show the Add to Compare button.

kind.description: What the section is. `setting` for all seven sections.

writable.description: Whether you can write to the section. `true` for all seven sections.

plugin.description: The plugin behind the section. Only `review_and_ratings` has it, set to `product-review`.

available.description: Whether that plugin is available. Only the entry that has `plugin` has it.

href.description: The section's own path, such as `/api/v4/admin/settings/page_settings/product_page/up_sell`.

description.description: What the field does.

type.description: The kind of value the field takes: `boolean`, `enum`, `integer`, `string` or `reference_list`.

default.description: The field's default value.

read_only.description: Whether the field is read-only. `true` only on `review_and_ratings.capabilities.available`.

depends_on.description: The field this one depends on, such as `quick_view.product_quick_view`. In `up_sell` and `related_products` it is the field name alone, such as `display_rating`. A write that sets this field to `true` while that field is off is rejected with `400`.

min.description: The lowest value, for an `integer` field.

max.description: The highest value, for an `integer` field.

item_shape.description: The shape of each item, for a `reference_list` field: `{id,name}`.

SearchResultProductInformation.description: Each search result, and how the result list displays, pages and sorts. The only section you can write.

use_default_product_listing_configuratio.description: Use the store's default product listing settings for the search result page.

display_content_page.description: Show content pages on the search result page.

display_loyalty_points.description: Show loyalty points on each result.

display_add_to_wishlist_button.description: Show the Add to Wishlist button.

enabled.description: Page the search results.

items_per_page.description: Items per page. At least `5`: a lower value is rejected with `400` and `items_per_page must be >= 5`, and a number with a fraction with `400` and `must be an integer`.

select_pagination_position.description: Where the pagination control shows, such as `bottom`. A value the store does not accept is rejected with `400` and `invalid enum value for select_pagination_position`.

allow_users_to_select_number_of_products.description: Let shoppers choose how many products a page shows.

number_of_products_per_load.description: Products added each time a shopper loads more.

updated.description: When the promotion was last changed.
