A create rejects a value that is not a real date and time in that form with `400`; a replace stores such a value as `null`. A replace without it sets it to `null`.

is_specify_end_date.description: Whether the profile has an `end_date`. A string such as `"yes"` is rejected with `400`, on create and on replace.

end_date.description: When the discount ends, written like `start_date`. A create stores it only when `is_specify_end_date` is `true`, and then rejects an `end_date` before `start_date` with `400`; a replace stores an earlier `end_date` as sent. A replace without it sets it to `""`.

is_apply_coupon_code.description: Whether the profile uses coupon codes. On create, `true` without a `default_coupon_code` makes the store generate one. [Generate coupon codes](/api-reference/discount-profiles/generate-coupon-codes) works only when this is `true`. A replace that sets it to `true` returns `customer_coupons` as `[]`: retrieve the profile to read its codes.

default_coupon_code.description: The profile's default coupon code. On create, a code another coupon already has is rejected with `400` and the message `Coupon code#<code> already exists`. A replace without it keeps the current code. On a replace that sets `is_apply_coupon_code` to `true`, `""` or `null` makes the store generate a new code in its place; without that flag, `""` keeps the current code.

is_coupon_code_auto_generate.description: Whether coupon codes are generated automatically.

is_create_unique_coupon_each_customer.description: Whether each customer gets a unique coupon code.

is_imported_coupon.description: Whether the coupon codes are imported. A string is rejected with `400`, on create and on replace.

is_maximum_use_total.description: Whether the discount has a total use limit, set in `maximum_use_count`. `is_maximum_use_limit` is accepted as another name.

maximum_use_count.description: The total number of uses allowed. `maximum_use_limit` is accepted as another name. A replace without it sets it to `null`.

is_maximum_use_customer.description: Whether each customer has a use limit, set in `maximum_use_customer_count`. `is_maximum_use_limit_by_customer` is accepted as another name.

maximum_use_customer_count.description: The number of uses allowed for each customer. `maximum_use_limit_by_customer` is accepted as another name. A replace without it sets it to `null`.

is_maximum_discount_allowed.description: Whether the discount has a maximum amount, set in `maximum_discount_allowed_amount`.

maximum_discount_allowed_amount.description: The maximum discount amount allowed. `maximum_discount_allowed` is accepted as another name. A replace without it sets it to `null`.

is_exclude_products_on_sale.description: Whether products on sale are excluded from the discount.

is_discount_used_with_other_discount.description: Whether the discount can be used with other discounts.

is_display_discount_information_prod_det.description: Whether discount information shows on the product detail page.

display_text_coupon.description: The coupon display text. A replace without it keeps the text, and `""` clears it.

display_text_cart.description: The cart display text. A replace without it keeps the text, and `""` clears it.

display_text_partial_discount_condition.description: The partial discount condition display text. A replace without it keeps the text, and `""` clears it.

invoice_note.description: A note for the invoice. A replace without it keeps the note, and `null` clears it.

exclude_products.description: The `id` of each product the discount excludes. Every entry must be an existing product's `id`: one that no product has returns `500` and stores nothing. A numeric string is read as the number, and a product `id` sent twice is kept twice. A replace without it keeps the list, and `[]` clears it.

DiscountProfileAmountDetails.description: The details block of an `amount` profile. A `single` block without `type`, `apply_to`, `single_amount` or `single_amount_type` returns `500` and stores nothing. `amount` and `amount_type` are accepted as other names for `single_amount` and `single_amount_type`, on create and on replace; when you send both names, `amount` and `amount_type` win.

type.description: `single` for one amount, or `tiered`.

apply_to.description: What the discount applies to, such as `total_order`.

single_amount.description: The discount amount, returned as a decimal such as `40.0`. A create rejects a negative value, or a `PERCENT` value above `100`, with `400` and the reason `out_of_range`; a replace stores it. A `tiered` block does not need it.

single_amount_type.description: `FLAT` or `PERCENT`. A create rejects any other value with `400` and the reason `invalid_enum`; a replace stores it.

tiers.description: Tier records you send are dropped: the profile returns `type: "tiered"` and `tiers: []`, so you cannot set tiers through the API. A profile whose tiers were set outside the API returns the `id` of each tier here, not the tier itself.

DiscountProfileShippingDetails.description: The details block of a `shipping` profile. Without `apply_to` or `minimum_qty_on`, the call returns `500` and stores nothing.

type.description: The shipping discount's type, such as `free_shipping`. It is not checked: any value is stored as sent.

apply_to.description: Required. What the discount applies to, such as `total_order`.

minimum_qty.description: The minimum quantity, stored as sent.

minimum_amount.description: The minimum amount, stored as sent and returned as a decimal such as `50.0`.

single_amount.description: In a `free_shipping` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

cap_amount.description: In a `free_shipping` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

maximum_time.description: In a `free_shipping` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

DiscountProfileProductDetails.description: The details block of a `product` profile. A create without `free_product_min_qty_on` returns `500` and stores nothing. A create whose block has keys the store does not recognise can return `500` and still store the profile.

type.description: The product discount's type, such as `free_product`.

free_product_min_amount.description: Stored as sent and returned as a decimal such as `25.0`.

single_amount.description: In a `free_product` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

cap_price.description: In a `free_product` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

cap_price_max_qty.description: In a `free_product` block, returned as `null` even when you send a value.

product_ids.description: Accepted but not stored: returned as `[]`.

id.description: The coupon's own `id`, assigned by the store. No call takes it: [Assign a coupon code to a customer](/api-reference/discount-profiles/assign-a-coupon-code-to-a-customer) finds the coupon by its `code`.

code.description: The coupon code. Send it as `code` to [Assign a coupon code to a customer](/api-reference/discount-profiles/assign-a-coupon-code-to-a-customer).

customer_email.description: The email address of the customer the code is assigned to, spelled as in the customer's record, or `""` until a customer is assigned. Deleting that customer leaves it unchanged.

total.description: The number of profiles that match your filters. There is no count endpoint: `GET /admin/discount_profiles/count` is rejected with `400` and the reason `invalid_id`.

limit.description: The page size the store applied: the `limit` you sent, at most `20`, or `20` when you send none.

offset.description: The number of profiles skipped before this page.

count.description: The number of profiles on this page.

current_page.description: `offset` divided by `limit`, rounded down, plus one. On an empty page past the last profile, it is `total_pages` instead.

has_next.description: `true` when more profiles come after this page.

has_previous.description: `true` when `offset` is above `0`. On an empty page past the last profile, it is `false` even when `offset` is above `0`.

previous_page.description: The full URL of the previous page, with the filters you sent, or `null` on the first page.

next_page.description: The full URL of the next page, with the filters you sent, or `null` on the last page. It uses `offset`, even when you sent `page`.

DiscountProfileGroupMeta.description: Returned only by the listing, with one entry.

kind.description: `resource`.

writable.description: `true`: you can create, replace and delete discount profiles.

DiscountProfileFieldMetadata.description: Describes every field of a profile, one entry per field name: the 35 fields every profile has and the three details blocks. The listing and [Retrieve a discount profile](/api-reference/discount-profiles/retrieve-a-discount-profile) return the same block. Its descriptions are wrong in two places: the `type` entry says an omitted `type` is stored as `null`, but a profile created without one returns `""`; and the `shipping_details` and `product_details` entries say their fields are not validated, but a block without `apply_to`, `minimum_qty_on` or `free_product_min_qty_on` returns `500`.

DiscountProfileFieldMetadataEntry.description: Describes one field. Every entry has `type`.

type.description: The kind of value the field holds.

read_only.description: `true` on the entries for `id`, `customer_coupons`, `created_on` and `last_updated_on`, and on no other entry.

fields.description: On the `amount_details` entry, the six fields of the amount block: `type`, `apply_to`, `single_amount`, `single_amount_type`, `minimum_amount_on` and `tiers`.

DiscountProfileGenerateCodesInput.description: Send `requested_codes` at the top level of the body, not wrapped in a key.

requested_codes.description: Required. The number of codes to generate, `1` or more. A numeric string such as `"2"` is read as the number. `0` or a missing value is rejected with `Invalid request data`, and a negative number with `Invalid number of requested codes`.

message.description: `<n> new codes generated.`, where `<n>` is the number of codes.

codes.description: The new codes, all different, in the order they were generated. They are added to the end of the profile's `customer_coupons`.

DiscountProfileAssignInput.description: Send `code` and `email` at the top level of the body. A body wrapped in a key is rejected with `Code is required`.

code.description: Required. A coupon code generated for a profile, from `codes` in the response to [Generate coupon codes](/api-reference/discount-profiles/generate-coupon-codes) or from the profile's `customer_coupons`.

email.description: Required. The email address of an existing customer, in any letter case. A customer awaiting verification is accepted.

message.description: `customer has been assigned successfully.`

DiscountProfileAssignError.description: The flat error body that [Assign a coupon code to a customer](/api-reference/discount-profiles/assign-a-coupon-code-to-a-customer) returns. It has no `error` object.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `Error customer assign to code`.

detailsMessage.description: The reason, such as `customer.not.found` when no customer has the `email` you sent, or `coupon.not.found.by.code` when no coupon has the `code` you sent.

DiscountProfileError.description: The error body of every discount profile call except [Assign a coupon code to a customer](/api-reference/discount-profiles/assign-a-coupon-code-to-a-customer), which returns a flat body instead.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `conflict` or `internal_error`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `Discount Profile not found` or `Discount Name already exists`.

details.description: More about the rejection. For a rejected field, each entry's `code` gives the reason, such as `invalid_enum`, `out_of_range`, `invalid_date`, `invalid_range`, `invalid_boolean` or `required`.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected, such as `sort`, or `id` when `discount_profile_id` is not a number.

code.description: Why the field was rejected.

message.description: What was wrong with the value, such as `must be a numeric discount profile id`. `null` when the listing rejects `limit`, `offset`, `page` or `sort`.

value.description: The value you sent, such as `NAME` for a rejected `sort`.

Blog.description: One blog post. A listing entry, a retrieve, and the response to a create, a replace or an update return the same seventeen fields.

id.description: The blog post's `id`, assigned by the store. Pass it as `blog_id` in a path.

title.description: The post's title, 2 to 255 characters once trimmed. No two blog posts, live or in the trash, have the same title in any letter case.

url.description: The post's URL slug, such as `spring-sale-announcement`. A create makes it from `title`: lower case, with spaces turned into hyphens and `-1` added when another post already has that slug. A later change of `title` alone does not change it; a replace that sends `url`, or an update that sends `url` beside `title`, sets it.

content.description: The post's body, as sent, or `null` when none is set.

date.description: The post's date, written `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss` with no time zone. A `date` sent as `2026-09-28` reads `2026-09-28T00:00:00`, and `2026-09-28T10:11:12Z` reads `2026-09-28T10:11:12`.

is_published.description: Whether the post is published. A create or replace that leaves it out sets it to `false`.

visibility.description: Who can see the post: `open`, `hidden` or `restricted`. Some existing posts read `OPEN` in upper case.

visible_to.description: `all` or `selected` on a restricted post, and `null` on a post that is `open` or `hidden`.

categories.description: The blog categories the post is filed under. A post created without `categories` is filed under the store's default category. Some existing posts read `[]`.

created_on.description: When the post was created, such as `2026-10-07T09:15:02`.

is_disposable.description: Set by the store: a write that sends it is rejected with `400`.

is_in_trash.description: `false` on a post you create. A write that sends it is rejected with `400`.

image.description: The post's cover image, or `{}` when it has none.

created_by.description: Who created the post, or `{}` on some existing posts. A write that sends it is rejected with `400`.

selected_customers.description: The audience of a restricted post: `[]`, a list, while it names no one, and an object holding `customers` and `groups` once it names anyone.

BlogCategoryReference.description: A blog category the post is filed under.

id.description: The blog category's `id`.

name.description: The blog category's name.

BlogImage.description: The cover image. `{}` when the post has none; otherwise all four keys.

file_name.description: The image's file name: the `file_name` sent with the upload, or a name the store chose when the upload sent `filename` instead.

link.description: Where the image is served: one URL whose path ends in the file name. Its query string changes on every read, so compare links without it.

id.description: The creator's `id`.

name.description: The creator's name.

BlogAudience.description: The customers and customer groups a restricted post is shown to.

customers.description: One entry per customer: the customer's `internal_id` as `id`, and the customer's first and last name as `name`.

groups.description: One entry per customer group: the group's `id` and `name`.

id.description: For a customer, the customer's `internal_id`; for a customer group, the group's `id`.

name.description: The customer's or customer group's name.

BlogSeoConfigs.description: The post's SEO meta tags, the same on a write and a read. Other keys inside it are ignored on a write.

meta_tag.description: One entry per meta tag. A post without any reads `[]`.

name.description: The meta tag's name, such as `description`.

value.description: The meta tag's value.

BlogGroupMeta.description: Describes the blog posts collection. Returned by the listing, a retrieve and an update, but not by a create or a replace.

kind.description: What the collection is: `resource`.

writable.description: Whether you can write to the collection: `true`.

total.description: The number of blog posts that match your filters, across all pages.

limit.description: The page size applied: the `limit` you sent, at most `20`, or `20` when you sent none.

offset.description: The number of posts skipped before this page.

count.description: The number of posts on this page.

current_page.description: The page that `offset` falls in, counting from `1`.

has_next.description: `true` when more posts follow this page.

previous_page.description: The full URL of the previous page, with your query, or `null` when `has_previous` is `false`.

next_page.description: The full URL of the next page, with your query, or `null` when `has_next` is `false`.

BlogFieldMetadata.description: One entry for each of the seventeen fields of a blog post, keyed by field name. Returned only when you send `field_metadata=true` to the listing or a retrieve. Some of its notes differ from what the store does: `url` is marked `read_only`, but a replace that sends `url`, or an update that sends it beside `title`, sets it; `title` is described as unique among live posts, but a post in the trash keeps its title taken too; and `visible_to` is described as required when `visibility` is `restricted`, but a create without it is accepted.

BlogFieldMetadataEntry.description: Describes one field. `type` and `note` are always present; the other keys only where they apply.

type.description: The field's value type.

note.description: What the field holds and how a write treats it.

required.description: Whether a write must send the field.

read_only.description: Whether the field is marked as not writable.

default.description: The value used when a write leaves the field out.

item_type.description: The type of each item, for a list field.

BlogInput.description: Send these fields inside `blog`. A create needs `title`; a replace needs `title` and `visibility` and resets most fields it leaves out; an update changes only the fields it sends. Any other field, including `created_on`, `created_by`, `is_disposable` and `is_in_trash`, is rejected with `400`. An `id` field here returns `500` on a create and is ignored on a replace or an update.

title.description: Required on create and replace. 2 to 255 characters once trimmed. No other blog post, live or in the trash, can have the same title in any letter case.

url.description: Ignored on create, where the store makes `url` from `title`. A replace sets it, and an update sets it only when you send `title` too. The store makes it lower case, turns spaces into hyphens and adds `-1` when another post has it. An empty value is ignored.

content.description: Free text, saved as sent. A create or replace that leaves it out sets it to `null`.

date.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 date and time, such as `2026-09-28` or `2026-09-28T10:11:12Z`. A create or replace that leaves it out sets it to the current time. Any other form is rejected with `400` (`invalid_date`).

is_published.description: `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`. A create or replace that leaves it out sets it to `false`. A string, `"true"` included, is rejected with `400` (`invalid_boolean`).

visibility.description: `open`, `hidden` or `restricted`, in lower case: `OPEN` is rejected with `400` (`invalid_enum`). Defaults to `open` on create. Required on replace.

visible_to.description: `all` or `selected`. Kept only while `visibility` is `restricted`; with `open` or `hidden` the post reads `null`. Any other value is rejected with `400` (`invalid_enum`).

categories.description: The blog categories to file the post under, each as an object holding the blog category's `id`, such as `{"id": 31}`. A bare number such as `[31]` returns `500`, and a blog category `id` that matches no blog category is rejected with `400` (`invalid_reference`). Sent as `[]`, or left out of a create or replace, the post is filed under the store's default category.

BlogCategoryRefInput.description: A blog category to file the post under. Other keys in the entry are ignored.

id.description: The blog category's `id`.

BlogImageInput.description: A cover image to upload. Nothing changes without `base64`: `{}`, `null` or a new `title` alone leaves the current image as it is. No call removes an image.

file_name.description: The name to save the file under. `filename` is accepted instead, but the store then chooses the name itself.

base64.description: The image file, base64-encoded. A new `base64` replaces the current image.

BlogAudienceInput.description: Who a restricted post is shown to. Needed when `visibility` is `restricted` and `visible_to` is `selected`: without anyone in it, the write is rejected with `400`. With `visibility` `open`, or `visible_to` `all`, the audience is dropped and reads `[]`.

customers.description: Each customer's `internal_id`, from [List customers](/api-reference/customers/list-customers). A customer's `customer_id` here is dropped without an error.

BlogComment.description: One comment on a blog post. The comment listing, a retrieve, and the response to adding, approving or marking a comment as spam return the same twelve fields.

id.description: The comment's `id`, assigned by the store. Pass it as `blog_comment_id` in a path.

status.description: `pending` on a new comment, `approved` after [Approve a comment](/api-reference/blogs/approve-a-comment), and `spam` after marking it as spam. A `status` sent when adding the comment is stored as sent.

name.description: The commenter's name, or `null` when none was sent.

email.description: The commenter's email address, or `null` when none was sent.

post_title.description: The blog post's current `title`. It changes when the post's title changes.

spam.description: `true` after the comment is marked as spam. Approving the comment does not set it back to `false`.

created_on.description: When the comment was added, such as `2026-10-07T09:30:12`.

replies.description: `[]` on a new comment. No call on this API adds a reply.

BlogCommentInput.description: Send these fields inside `blog` and then `comment`. Fields the store does not recognise are dropped, and so are the `id`, `spam`, `likes`, `total_reply` and `post_title` fields. Leave out `status`, which is stored as sent, and `replies`, which returns `500` when it is not empty.

content.description: Required. At most 1000 characters; blank is rejected with `400`.

name.description: Optional. 2 to 100 characters once trimmed.

email.description: Optional. A malformed address is rejected with `400` (`invalid_email`).

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request` or `not_found`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `blog info missing` or `Blog not found`.

details.description: One entry per rejected field or query parameter, or an empty list. A rejected `dir` is not named in it.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `unknown_parameter`, `unknown_field`, `out_of_range`, `invalid_sort_field` or `invalid_boolean`.

message.description: `null` when the listing, the count or a retrieve rejects a query parameter.

value.description: The value you sent, such as `title` for a rejected `sort`, `True` for a rejected `field_metadata`, or the number `0` for `limit=0`. Left out when the listing does not accept the parameter at all.

BlogServerError.description: The body of a `500`. It has no `error` object.

code.description: Always `500`.

message.description: Always `Unexpected Error Occurred`.

BlogCategory.description: One blog category. A listing entry, a retrieve, a create and an update return the same ten fields.

id.description: The blog category's `id`, assigned by the store. Pass it as `blog_category_id` in a path.

name.description: The category's name, 2 to 255 characters. No two blog categories have the same name.

url.description: The category's URL slug, such as `seasonal-promotions`. A create without one gets a `url` made from `name`, and a `url` another category already has is saved with `-1` added to the end.

description.description: The category's description, saved as sent, HTML included. `""` when none is set.

is_disposable.description: `false` on a category you create. A create ignores a value you send for it.

is_in_trash.description: `false` on a category you create. A create ignores a value you send for it.

image.description: The category's image, or `{}` when it has none.

created_on.description: When the category was created, in UTC, written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` without a time zone, such as `2026-07-16T06:24:24`. An update never changes it.

last_updated_on.description: When the category last changed, written like `created_on`. On a new category it equals `created_on` or is one second later, so do not expect the two to match. An update changes it only when a value changed.

seo_configs.description: The category's SEO entries. You cannot set them through this API: a category you create has `[]`, and a create or update that sends `seo_configs` stores nothing.

BlogCategoryImage.description: An uploaded image. `{}` when the category has no image; otherwise all four keys.

title.description: The image title, or `""` when the upload sent none.

alternative_text.description: The image's alternative text, or `""` when the upload sent none.

file_name.description: The `file_name` sent with the upload, or a name the store chose when the upload sent none.

link.description: Where the image is served. An upload made through the API is served from your store's own host at `/resources/<store id>/blog-category/category-<blog_category_id>/450-<file_name>`; some categories link to a CDN copy whose name differs from `file_name`. The link ends in a query string that changes on every read, so compare links without it. Once the category is deleted, the link returns `404`.

BlogCategorySeoConfig.description: One SEO entry of a blog category.

id.description: The SEO entry's `id`.

value.description: The entry's value, as text.

type.description: The entry's type, such as `page_seo`.

BlogCategoryInput.description: Send these fields inside `blog_category`, on a create and on an update. A create ignores unknown fields and the fields you cannot write here: `is_disposable`, `is_in_trash`, `created_on`, `last_updated_on` and `seo_configs`. An update ignores `seo_configs` too. Do not send the category's `id`: inside `blog_category`, it returns `500` on a create and is ignored on an update.

name.description: Required on create and update, 2 to 255 characters. A `name` another blog category already has is rejected with `400`.

url.description: Optional. The store lowercases it, turns each run of characters other than ASCII letters, digits and `_` into one hyphen, drops a hyphen at either end and cuts it to 50 characters. On a create without it, the store makes it from `name` the same way. A `url` another blog category already has is saved with `-1` added to the end. On an update, sending the category's current `url` keeps it as it is, and a `url` you leave out, or send as `""` or `null`, keeps its value.

description.description: Optional. Saved as sent, HTML included, and `""` when you leave it out. On an update, a `description` you leave out, or send as `null`, is saved as `""`.

image.description: Optional. An image to upload. On an update, an `image` you leave out, or send as `{}` or `null`, keeps the current image.

blogs.description: Optional. Blog posts to file under the category. On a create, each post then lists the category in its `categories`. On an update, `blogs` left out or sent as `[]` keeps every link.

BlogCategoryImageInput.description: An image upload. Nothing in `image` is stored without `base64`.

file_name.description: The name to save the file under. Without it, the store chooses a name.

base64.description: The image file, base64-encoded, without a `data:` prefix: a value such as `data:image/png;base64,...` is rejected with `400`. On an update, a new `base64` replaces the current image.

title.description: The image title. Saved only with a `base64` in the same request; otherwise ignored, on a create and on an update.

alternative_text.description: The image's alternative text. Saved only with a `base64` in the same request; otherwise ignored.

BlogCategoryBlogLink.description: A blog post to file under the category.

id.description: The blog post's `id`.

total.description: The number of blog categories in the listing, across all pages.

limit.description: The page size the store applied: the `limit` you sent, at most `20`, or `20` when you sent none.

offset.description: The number of categories skipped before this page.

count.description: The number of categories on this page.

current_page.description: The number of this page, counting from `1`. Past the last category it does not follow `page`: `page=2` with 20 or fewer categories returns `1`.

has_next.description: `true` when more categories follow this page.

has_previous.description: `true` when categories come before this page. `false` on a page past the last category, such as `page=2` with 20 or fewer categories.

previous_page.description: The full URL of the previous page, with `limit` and `offset`, or `null` when `has_previous` is `false`.

next_page.description: The full URL of the next page, with `limit` and `offset`, or `null` when `has_next` is `false`.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed` or `internal_error`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `blog category not found`.

details.description: Names the rejected field when the listing rejects `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `sort` or a parameter it does not accept, or when a write rejects a missing or too-long `name`. An empty list on every other error, including a rejected `dir` and a `name` another category already has.

field.description: The query parameter or body field that was rejected, such as `limit`, `sort` or `name`.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `unknown_parameter`, `invalid_sort_field`, `out_of_range`, `invalid_integer`, `required` or `invalid_length`.

message.description: `null` when the listing rejects a query parameter. When a write rejects `name`, the reason without the field name, such as `is required`.

value.description: The value you sent, such as `abc` or `created_on`. On the `out_of_range` error for `limit=0` it is the number `0`; on the `invalid_integer` error for `limit=-1` it is the string `"-1"`. On a `name` rejected for its length, it is the number of characters you sent. Absent on a parameter the listing does not accept and on a missing `name`.

Product.description: One product: 69 fields, the same set on every product.

id.description: The product's `id`. Pass it as `product_id` in a path. Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

status.description: Read-only: sending it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

urls.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

parents.description: The categories the product is filed under. In a write, send their ids as a list of numbers.

created_by.description: Who created the product. Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

created_at.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

updated_at.description: Changes when the product changes. A value you send is ignored.

product_page.description: The product's page as `id` and `name`. Some products return `{}` instead.

custom_class.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

available_for.description: Who can buy the product. `selected` limits it to the customers and groups in `selected_customers`.

selected_customers.description: The customers and customer groups the product is available to, as an object with `customers` and `groups`, or `[]` when the product names none.

password.description: `***` when the product has a password, `""` when it has none. Sending back `***` keeps the stored password.

sold_out.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

length.description: Read-only here: write it in `product_properties`. A changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

width.description: Read-only here: write it in `product_properties`. A changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

height.description: Read-only here: write it in `product_properties`. A changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

weight.description: Read-only here: write it in `product_properties`. A changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

sold_out_label.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

featured.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

new.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

model.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

version.description: Changes when the product changes, including when its stock changes. A write that changes nothing keeps it. A value you send is ignored.

created_on.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

last_updated_on.description: Changes when the product changes. A value you send is ignored.

last_updated_by.description: Who last changed the product, or `null`. Changes when the product changes. A value you send is ignored.

is_draft.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

reviews.description: Read-only: sending it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

product_variation.description: The product's variation types and variants, or `{}` on a product with no variations.

has_variations.description: Read-only: a changed value is rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field`.

ProductNamedReference.description: A record the product refers to: an author, a page, a customer or a customer group.

id.description: The `id` of the named person, page, customer or customer group.

ProductParent.description: One category the product is filed under. [List categories](/api-reference/categories/list-categories) returns the store's categories.

id.description: The category's id.

customers.description: The customers the product is available to.

groups.description: The customer groups the product is available to.

ProductWeekday.description: One day of the weekday schedule.

weekdays.description: One entry per day in the schedule, or `[]` when `enabled` is `false`.

ProductProperties.description: The product's dimensions. Write them here; the product's top-level `length`, `width`, `height` and `weight` repeat them and are read-only.

ProductTaxSettings.description: Tax settings for this product. They apply only when `overwrite_default_config` is `true`.

ProductVariationPriceDisplay.description: Which variant price a listing shows, and its labels.

ProductWarehouseStock.description: One location's units, in an older format.

warehouse.description: The inventory location's id, as text, such as `"4"`. Every other location id in these responses is a number.

ProductStockLocation.description: One inventory location the product is assigned to.

warehouse.description: The inventory location's id. Pass it as `inventory_location_id` to unassign the location.

stock.description: The units of the product at this location.

low_stock_level.description: The low-stock level at this location, or `null` when it was set without one.

is_default.description: `true` on the product's default location. Exactly one row has it.

ProductPricingAndStock.description: The product's pricing and stock settings.

available_stock.description: The sum of `stock` over the product's locations.

low_level_stock.description: Takes the `low_stock_level` of the product's default location.

warehouses.description: The same units as `locations`, with each location id as text.

locations.description: The same rows as `locations` in [Retrieve a product's stock](/api-reference/products/retrieve-a-products-stock).

id.description: The image's id.
The video's id.

ProductAdvanceInformation.description: The product's identifiers and origin. An update that names one of these fields keeps the others.

mpn.description: Write it here: at the top level of the product it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

upc.description: Write it here: at the top level of the product it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

barcode.description: Write it here: at the top level of the product it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

hs_code.description: Write it here: at the top level of the product it is rejected with `400` and the reason `unknown_field`.

id.description: The linked product's id.

ProductSeoConfig.description: One SEO setting on the product.

id.description: The SEO setting's id.
The tag value's id.

ProductTag.description: One tag on the product, with its values.

id.description: The `id` of this entry in the product's `tags`.
The custom property's id.
The review's id.

productId.description: The reviewed product's id. This is the only camelCase field name in the product.

id.description: The option's id.

ProductVariationType.description: One variation type the product uses, with its options.

id.description: The variation type's id.
The variation type's id.
The option's id.

type.description: A list of one entry: the variation type the option belongs to.

id.description: The image's id.

ProductCombinationPriceAndStock.description: A variant's pricing and stock settings.

weight.description: A number on some products and text on others.

height.description: A number on some products and text on others.

length.description: A number on some products and text on others.

width.description: A number on some products and text on others.

ProductCombination.description: One combination of options and the variant it makes.

ProductVariation.description: `{}` on a product with no variations.

ProductInput.description: Send these fields at the top level of the body, not inside `product`. Only the fields you send change, inside nested blocks too. A read-only field from [Retrieve a product](/api-reference/products/retrieve-a-product) is accepted when its value is unchanged and rejected with `400` and the reason `read_only_field` when it differs. `status` and `reviews` are rejected with the reason `unknown_field`. `updated_at`, `version`, `last_updated_on` and `last_updated_by` are ignored.

available_from_date.description: Sent on its own, it is ignored.

available_to_date.description: Sent on its own, it is ignored.

password.description: Send `***` to keep the stored password. Sent on its own, it is ignored.

parents.description: The ids of the categories to file the product under.

ProductStockVariation.description: One variant's stock, on a product with variations.

product_id.description: The variant's own product `id`. It differs from the `product_id` in the path.

ProductStock.description: A product's stock at each inventory location it is assigned to.

product_id.description: The product's id, the `product_id` in the path.

multi_location_enabled.description: `false` on a product with no location. Assigning the product's first location sets it to `true`.

available_stock.description: The sum of `stock` over the rows in `locations`.

locations.description: One row per inventory location the product is assigned to, or `[]` when it has none.

variations.description: Only on a product with variations: one entry per variant.

ProductStockLocationInput.description: One location the product keeps. Other keys, such as `warehouse_name`, are ignored.

warehouse.description: Required. The inventory location's id, as a number or as numeric text. [List inventory locations](/api-reference/inventory-locations/list-inventory-locations) returns the store's locations.

stock.description: The units at this location, `0` or more.

low_stock_level.description: The low-stock level at this location. Left out or `null`, it is stored as `null`.

is_default.description: Send `true` on the row for the product's default location. When no row has it, the first row you send becomes the default.

ProductStockInput.description: Send these fields at the top level of the body.

note.description: Optional. It changes nothing you can read back in the response or on the product.

locations.description: Required and not empty. Replaces the product's whole set of locations: a location you leave out is unassigned, even while it holds stock.

ProductFieldMetadata.description: Returned beside `product` when you send `field_metadata=true` or `1`. An object keyed by field name, such as `id`: `{"type": "integer", "read_only": true}`. The `password` entry has `write_only: true`. It lists `mpn`, `upc`, `barcode`, `hs_code`, `length`, `width`, `height`, `weight` and `sold_out_label` as writable at the top level, but an update rejects each of them there.

ProductError.description: Rejections return this shape. A method a path does not support is rejected too: `HEAD` on a product returns `404` although its `Allow` header lists `HEAD`; `HEAD`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `OPTIONS` on a product's `stock` return `404` with the message `No such endpoint: <METHOD> /api/v4/admin/products/<product_id>/stock`; and `GET` on `stock/locations/{inventory_location_id}` returns `405` with the reason `method_not_allowed`.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `conflict`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `locations is required`.

details.description: One entry per rejected field or parameter, or an empty list.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `unknown_parameter`, `has_stock` or `is_default`.

value.description: The value involved, when the API includes it, such as the inventory location's id on `has_stock`.

id.description: The variation type's `id`, set by the store. Pass it as `variation_id` in a path. Read-only.

name.description: The type's name, 2 to 100 characters. No two types have the same name, in any letter case.

standard.description: The kind of type: `text`, `color` or `image`. It cannot change after the type is created.

disposable.description: Read-only. `false` on a type you create.

id.description: The option's `id`, set by the store. Pass it as `variation_option_id` to delete the option, or send it as the option's `id` in a replace or update to change the option.

label.description: The option's label, unique within its type.

value.description: The option's value. On a `color` type, a colour such as `#ff0000` or `rgb(0,0,255)`. `null` on an `image` option.

order.description: The option's order number, from `0` to `999`.

default.description: `true` on the type's default option. At most one option has it.

image.description: The option's picture on an `image` type, or `null` on a `text` or `color` type.

url.description: The full address of the stored picture.

file_name.description: The `filename` you sent with the picture.

VariationInput.description: Send these fields inside `variation`. Create requires `name`, `standard` and `options`; replace requires `name` and `options`; update takes any of them.

name.description: 2 to 100 characters, trimmed. A name another type has, in any letter case, is rejected with `409`.

standard.description: `text`, `color` or `image`, in any letter case; stored in lower case. Leave it out on replace and update, or send the type's own value: a different value is rejected with `400`.

options.description: 1 to 1000 options. On replace, this is the full list: options you leave out are deleted.

id.description: Send the `id` of one of this type's options to change that option. Leave it out to add a new option.

value.description: Trimmed. On a `color` type, a hex value, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()`, `hsv()` or a colour name. Leave it out on an `image` option.

default.description: Optional. `true` makes this the type's default option and takes the flag off the option that had it.

VariationOptionImageInput.description: An option's picture on an `image` type. The response returns it as `image.url` and `image.file_name`.

filename.description: The picture's file name, such as `swatch.png`.

total.description: The number of variation types that match your request.

limit.description: The page size applied: the `limit` you sent, or `20`.

offset.description: The number of types skipped before this page.

has_previous.description: `true` when `offset` is above `0`. It is `false` when `offset` is past the last type.

has_next.description: `true` when there is a page after this one.

VariationFieldMetadata.description: Describes the five fields of a variation type, keyed by field name. Each entry gives the field's `type`. `id` and `disposable` have `read_only` set to `true`. `standard` lists `text`, `color` and `image` in `values`. `options` has `min_items` `1`, `max_items` `1000` and a `fields` block that describes the six option fields.

variations.description: The product's variant groups. Empty for a product without variants.

product_key.description: The product's variation type names joined with `/`, such as `Size/Colour`.

variation_id.description: Identifies the variant. It is not a variation type's `id`. Send it in `variation_ids` to update the variant.

key.description: The variant's option labels joined with `/`, such as `Small/Red`.

name.description: The variant's name.

VariationProductVariantPricing.description: On a product whose prices include tax, `base_price` and `sale_price` are the stored prices divided by the tax rate and rounded to the cent.

is_on_sale.description: Whether the variant is on sale.

is_enabled.description: Whether inventory tracking is on for the variant.

quantity.description: The variant's stock. `available_stock` in an update sets it, even when tracking is off.

min_quantity.description: The smallest quantity a customer can order.

max_quantity.description: The largest quantity a customer can order. `0` means no maximum.

weight.description: A number, or a numeric string such as `"26.455471"`. Read both forms.

id.description: The image's `id`.

url.description: The full address of the image.

thumbnail.description: The full address of the image's thumbnail.

VariationBulkInput.description: Send these fields at the top level of the body, with no wrapper. Send `variation_ids` and at least one other field. Other fields are ignored.

variation_ids.description: The `variation_id` of each variant to update, as numbers or numeric strings such as `"22"`. Every one must be a variant of the product whose `product_id` is in the path.

base_price.description: The base price to store, as sent. On a product whose prices include tax, send the price including tax.

cost_price.description: The cost price to store, as sent.

available_stock.description: Sets each variant's `inventory.quantity`, even when inventory tracking is off.

max_order_quantity.description: Sets each variant's `ordering.max_quantity`. `0` means no maximum.

message.description: The number of variants updated, such as `1 variations updated`.

failed.description: An empty list. When an entry in `variation_ids` is not a variant of the product, the whole request is rejected with `400` instead.

VariationBulkUpdate.description: One updated variant. Only `id` and `name` unless you send `response=full`.

id.description: The variant's `variation_id`.

name.description: The variant's name.

options.description: The options that make up the variant.

url.description: A path such as `/api/v4/admin/products/4321/variations/91`. Calling it returns `404` with the message `No such endpoint`.

id.description: The variation option's `id`.

VariationBulkPricing.description: `base_price` is the price as stored, including tax on a product whose prices include tax. `sale_price` and `is_on_sale` can differ from what [List a product's variants](/api-reference/variations/list-a-products-variants) returns for a product on sale.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `conflict`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `Variation not found`.

details.description: One entry per rejected field or parameter, or an empty list.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `unknown_field`, `invalid_enum` or `last_option`.

message.description: Why the field or parameter was rejected, or `null`.

value.description: The value you sent, when a value was rejected, such as `foo` for `standard`.

id.description: The country's numeric `id`. Pass it, the `code` or the `name` as `country_id` in a path.

code.description: The country's code: two upper-case letters, such as `AU`.

name.description: The country's name, such as `Australia`.

state_count.description: How many states the country has. It equals `pagination.total` from [List the states of a country](/api-reference/countries/list-the-states-of-a-country).

default.description: `true` only on the store's default country, the `default_country` in the `administration` site settings section.

CountryReference.description: The country a state list or a state belongs to.

id.description: The country's numeric `id`.

code.description: The country's two-letter code.

name.description: The country's name.

id.description: The state's numeric `id`. It is unique across all countries. Pass it, the `code` or the `name` as `state_id` in a path.

code.description: The state's code, such as `VIC`.

name.description: The state's name, such as `Victoria`.

default.description: `true` only on the store's default state, the `default_state` in the `administration` site settings section. `false` on every other state of every country.

total.description: The number of rows that match your request.

limit.description: The page size applied: the `limit` you sent, or `20`. With `limit=all`, the number of rows returned.

offset.description: The number of rows skipped before this page.

has_previous.description: `true` when there is a page before this one.

has_next.description: `true` when there is a page after this one.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `method_not_allowed`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `Country not found` or `1 parameter failed validation.`.

details.description: One entry per rejected query parameter. Empty on a `404` or a `405`.

field.description: The query parameter that was rejected.

code.description: Why the parameter was rejected, such as `out_of_range`, `invalid_enum` or `unsupported_parameter`.

message.description: What the parameter accepts, such as `must be true or false`.

value.description: The value you sent.

id.description: The currency's `id`, set by the store. Pass it as `currency_id` in the path of the other calls.

name.description: The currency's name, unique in any letter case.

code.description: Three upper-case letters, unique across the store's currencies.

conversion_rate.description: The currency's rate against the base currency, to at most 6 decimal places. `1` on the base currency. A whole number, such as `1`, is returned without a decimal point.

base.description: `true` on the store's base currency. Exactly one currency has it, and only [Set the base currency](/api-reference/currencies/set-the-base-currency) changes it.

updated_at.description: When the currency last changed, such as `2026-10-11T04:12:09Z`. Setting the base currency changes it on every currency.

CurrencyCountry.description: The country the currency belongs to.

id.description: The country's numeric `id`. A write can send it as `country`.

code.description: The country's two-letter code.

name.description: The country's name.

CurrencyInput.description: Send these fields at the top level of the body. Any other field, `id` included, is rejected with `400`.

name.description: At most 100 characters. No other currency may have the same name in any letter case. Spaces at either end are removed.

code.description: Three letters, stored in upper case. No other currency may have the same code. The store does not check it against ISO 4217.

symbol.description: At most 3 characters. Spaces at either end are removed.

country.description: The country's numeric `id`, its two-letter `code`, its `name`, or an object such as `{"code": "NZ"}`. Defaults to the store's default country. A country the store does not have is rejected with `400`.

conversion_rate.description: Above `0` and at most `999999999`. Stored to 6 decimal places, so `1.234567891` is stored as `1.234568`. Defaults to `1`.

active.description: Defaults to `true`. An inactive currency cannot be made the base.

CurrencyPatchInput.description: Send only the fields to change, at the top level of the body. Any other field, `id` included, is rejected with `400`, and so is an empty body.

name.description: At most 100 characters. No other currency may have the same name in any letter case. Spaces at either end are removed.

code.description: Three letters, stored in upper case. No other currency may have the same code. The store does not check it against ISO 4217.

symbol.description: At most 3 characters. Spaces at either end are removed.

country.description: The country's numeric `id`, its two-letter `code`, its `name`, or an object such as `{"code": "NZ"}`. Defaults to the store's default country. A country the store does not have is rejected with `400`.

conversion_rate.description: Above `0` and at most `999999999`. Stored to 6 decimal places, so `1.234567891` is stored as `1.234568`. Defaults to `1`.

active.description: Defaults to `true`. An inactive currency cannot be made the base.

total.description: The number of currencies that match your request.

limit.description: The page size applied: the `limit` you sent, or `20`.

offset.description: The number of currencies skipped before this page.

has_previous.description: `true` when `offset` is above `0`, even past the last currency.

has_next.description: `true` when there are currencies after this page.

total.description: The number of currencies that match `search` and `active`.

CurrencyReference.description: The currency that was the base before the change.

id.description: The previous base currency's `id`, which other calls take as `currency_id`.

code.description: The previous base currency's `code`.

name.description: The previous base currency's `name`.

currency.description: The new base currency. Only these four fields are returned.

id.description: The new base currency's `id`, the `currency_id` you sent.

previous_base.description: The currency that was the base, or `null` when the currency you named was already the base.

CurrencyFieldDescription.description: Describes one currency field. Other keys give the field's limits and default.

type.description: The field's value type: `string`, `reference`, `number`, `enum`, `integer`, `boolean` or `datetime`.

required.description: On the eight writable fields: `true` on `name`, `code` and `symbol`, and `false` on the others.

writable.description: `true` on the eight fields a write can set: `name`, `code`, `symbol`, `country`, `conversion_rate`, `rounding`, `precision` and `active`.

accepts.description: On `country`: `id`, `code`, `name` and `object`, the forms a write can send.

pattern.description: On `code`: `3 letters (ISO 4217), stored upper-case`. Any three letters are accepted.

note.description: On `base`: `change with PUT /api/v4/admin/currencies/{id}/base`, where `{id}` is the currency's `currency_id`.

CurrencyFieldMetadata.description: Describes each currency field, keyed by field name. Returned only when you send `field_metadata=true`.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `conflict`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `The base currency cannot be deleted.`

details.description: One entry per rejected field or parameter, or an empty list.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `required`, `unknown_field` or `duplicate`.

message.description: The reason in words, such as `is not a currency field`.

value.description: The value you sent for a rejected query parameter, such as `bogus` for `sort=bogus`.

TransactionListEntry.description: One row of the transactions list.

transaction_no.description: The transaction number. Pass it as `transaction_no` in a path.

total_records.description: How many records are stamped with the number. A record you delete stays counted.

url.description: The path of [Retrieve a transaction](/api-reference/transactions/retrieve-a-transaction) for this number. A space in the number appears as `+`, and the link then returns `404`.

TransactionTypeCount.description: One `by_type` row: the records of one type stamped with the number.

type.description: The record type. Pass it as `type` to [List the records of a transaction](/api-reference/transactions/list-the-records-of-a-transaction).

count.description: How many records of this type are stamped with the number.

items_url.description: The path of [List the records of a transaction](/api-reference/transactions/list-the-records-of-a-transaction) for this type. Present only when `count` is above `0`. A space in the number appears as `+`, and the link then returns `404`.

transaction_no.description: The transaction number you sent in the path.

total_records.description: How many records are stamped with the number, across all types.

TransactionItem.description: One record stamped with the number, as `detail=slim` returns it. Every item has `id`; the other fields depend on `type`: `category` has `name` and `url`; `product` and `product_variation` have `name`, `sku` and `url`; `product_review` has `name`, `rating` and `url`; `customer` has `email`, `first_name`, `last_name` and `url`; `order` has `order_no`, `grand_total`, `status` and `url`; `currency` has `name`, `code`, `symbol` and `url`; `custom_tax_profile` has `name`, `code` and `url`; `custom_tax_rule` has `name` only; `custom_tax_rule_zone` has `country_code`, `state_name`, `postcode`, `rate` and `priority`; `shipping_profile` has `name`, `description` and `url`; `shipping_rate` has `name`, `policy_type` and `url`. With `detail=full`, the item is the record's full body instead.

id.description: The record's `id`. Where the item has a `url`, the `id` is the last part of it, except for `order`: an order's `url` ends with its `order_no`, the value the orders API takes as `order_id`. For `category`, the `id` is the value [Retrieve a category](/api-reference/categories/retrieve-a-category) takes as `category_id`.

name.description: The record's name. Not returned for `customer`, `order` or `custom_tax_rule_zone`.

email.description: The email address of a `customer`, such as `jane@example.com`.

order_no.description: The order number of an `order`. The order's `url` ends with it.

code.description: The code of a `currency` or a `custom_tax_profile`.

state_name.description: The state name of a `custom_tax_rule_zone`, or `null` when the zone has no state.

description.description: The description of a `shipping_profile`.

url.description: The path you call to retrieve the record, such as `/api/v4/admin/products/207`. Not returned for `custom_tax_rule` or `custom_tax_rule_zone`.

total.description: The number of rows that match your request.

limit.description: The page size applied: the `limit` you sent, or `20`.

offset.description: The number of rows skipped before this page.

count.description: The number of rows on this page.

current_page.description: The page number of this page, counting from `1`. Past the last row, it equals `total_pages`.

total_pages.description: The number of pages at this `limit`.

has_next.description: `true` when there is a page after this one.

has_previous.description: `true` when there is a page before this one. Past the last row it is `false`, even though earlier rows exist.

previous_page.description: The absolute URL of the previous page, or `null`.

next_page.description: The absolute URL of the next page, or `null`. A space in the number appears as `+`, and the link then returns `404`; call the SDK function with the next `offset` instead.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, such as `invalid_request`, `not_found` or `method_not_allowed`.

message.description: What went wrong, such as `transaction not found` or `type query parameter is required`.

details.description: One entry per rejected query parameter or path value. Empty on a `405`.

field.description: The query parameter or path parameter that was rejected, such as `type` or `transaction_no`.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `required`, `out_of_range`, `invalid_value` or `not_found`.

message.description: What the parameter accepts, such as `max cannot exceed 200`, or `null`.

value.description: The value you sent. Not returned when the parameter is missing.

id.description: The alias's `id`, assigned by the store. Pass it as `alias_id` to delete the alias.

alias.description: The hostname, such as `shop.example.com`, with surrounding whitespace trimmed and the letter case you sent.

created_at.description: When the alias was created, such as `2026-08-31T11:57:23`. Set by the store: a value you send on create is ignored.

updated_at.description: Set by the store: a value you send on create is ignored. Equal to `created_at` on a new alias.

alias.description: Required. The hostname as a plain string, such as `shop.example.com`. It must be well formed, and no other alias may have it in any letter case. A record here is rejected with `400 invalid_hostname`.

total.description: The number of domain aliases in the store.

limit.description: The page size the store applied. At most `20`.

offset.description: The number of aliases skipped before this page.

has_next.description: `true` when more aliases follow this page.

code.description: The HTTP status, such as `404`.

message.description: What was wrong, such as `alias not found`.

error.description: A machine-readable reason, on some errors only: `method_not_allowed`, `unknown_parameter`, `invalid_pagination`, `invalid_number`, `invalid_hostname` or `empty_body`.

errors.description: Only on a `400` for a bad hostname or a bad query parameter. Each entry names the rejected `field` and a `code`.

field.description: The field or query parameter that was rejected, such as `alias` or `q`.

code.description: Why it was rejected, such as `invalid_hostname` or `unknown_parameter`.

message.description: On a bad hostname: `must be a well-formed hostname/FQDN (e.g. shop.example.com)`.

provided.description: On a bad hostname: the value you sent.
